messages:
Alex M: Heads up — customer POC hitting TLS handshake failures when hitting the private endpoint from their staging VPC. Error shows certificate CN mismatch. They can reach the IP but TLS fails. :confused:
Priya S: Can you paste the curl -v output? Also which hostname are they resolving to inside the VPC? Often private DNS points to the ENI IP not the public CN. :thinking:
Alex M: Curl shows TLS alert: "UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE" and server cert subject CN=my-api.prod.redwood-internal. Their app uses api.customer.example as SNI. They said internal DNS resolves api.customer.example -> 10.10.5.12.
Priya S: Two quick checks: 1) Is there a TLS-terminating proxy (ALB/NLB with TLS) in front? 2) Are they using our private endpoint (VPC endpoint) or an explicit peered VPC route? If cert CN is redwood-internal then SNI needs to match cert SAN or we need to present a cert that matches api.customer.example.
Jason L: If they're peering, confirm route table on the source subnet has a route to the peer and that security groups allow 443 egress. Also check if NAT gateway / egress rules are rewriting DNS or doing transparent TLS proxying. We've seen corporate egress devices replace certs.
Alex M: They're not using NAT for egress to the endpoint — it's entirely internal traffic. No internet path. Peering + private hosted zone. Security groups allow 443 outbound.
Priya S: Ok. Next: does the private hosted zone in Route53 have the exact record for api.customer.example in the customer's account or in Redwood's account? Split-horizon DNS can return different names. If the returned name doesn't match the cert SAN, handshake fails.
Katie R: Can we get the verbose openssl s_client output from their app host? Command to run on a test host:
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.12:443 -servername api.customer.example -showcerts
```
That will show the certificate chain and the presented CN/SANs.
Alex M: Pasting truncated openssl output: "subject=CN = my-api.prod.redwood-internal" and SAN has internal.redwood.net only. So mismatch. Customer says they control the DNS name and expect our endpoint to present their cert.
Priya S: Two approaches: a) Terminate TLS at their side (they present cert for api.customer.example) — they'd need a mutual TLS/ingress config with our private endpoint OR b) Use SNI routing on our side to present the correct cert — but that requires the cert to be uploaded or bound to the private endpoint/ALB. Which deployment mode are they on? Hosted private endpoint or dedicated?
Alex M: They're on Redwood Private (VPC package) with our private endpoint inside their account. They assumed our endpoint would automatically present the customer hostname cert.
Jason L: If it's in their account, they must attach the cert to the gateway/ALB in their VPC. In many setups we provision an internal ALB with the Redwood certificate. We can't issue a cert for customer domain unless they provide it or CNAME validation is done.
Katie R: I'll open a quick runbook thread for them. Steps: 1) verify the cert uploaded to their ALB or LB in the VPC 2) confirm Route53 private hosted zone returns the customer hostname 3) ensure client uses SNI matching uploaded cert 4) check SGs/RTs allow traffic. I'll request a support bundle (troubleshooting logs + openssl output).
Alex M: They've uploaded the cert to their internal ALB but still sees the same CN from the backend. Could it be that our agent is terminating and re-encrypting with our cert?
Priya S: If we have a sidecar or reverse-proxy in front of the service it may be terminating TLS and re-muting with our internal cert chain. Need to check the endpoint config: is TLS passthrough enabled or is it TLS terminated at the load balancer?
Jason L: Also check SNI forwarding on the ALB target group. Some older proxies ignore client SNI and present their own cert. If they want end-to-end cert, configure TCP (TLS passthrough) listeners instead of HTTPS listeners.
infra-bot: Related docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/private/vpc-endpoints#tls and https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/tls-passthrough :link: (auto-posted)
Katie R: Alex — can you collect a packet capture or run tcpdump on the client host and attach? Capture filter: `host 10.10.5.12 and port 443` and send pcap to support. Also include ALB listener config screenshots.
Alex M: Will collect and send. Customer also reported intermittent 429s earlier — could that be related? They see TLS handshake, then immediate rate-limit on our side.
Priya S: 429s could be from upstream rate limiting if requests are routed to a shared ingress before reaching the private instance. If TLS is failing and retried, it can look like bursts. We'll ask logs for X-Redwood-Route headers so we can track the request path.
Katie R: Noted. I'll triage both: TLS cert mismatch + 429. Putting together an action list and ETA for customer. :thumbsup:
Alex M: Thanks all — sending bundle now.
Priya S: Once we have pcap and s_client output we'll confirm whether TLS passthrough vs termination is needed and advise config change.
Katie R: I'll escalate to solutions-eng if we need a cert provisioning option.
Alex M: Closing loop once support case created (I'll post case number).
